t: Simple vs Compound Interest: Same Money, Very Different Result
d:
Simple interest and compound interest: same money, same rate, wildly different result.

$10,000 at 7% for 30 years becomes about $31,000 with simple interest and about $76,000 with compounding. No return is guaranteed, but compounding rewards time.

t: The Rule of 72: How Fast Your Money Doubles
d:
Want to know how fast your money doubles? The Rule of 72 does it in your head.

Divide 72 by your rate. At 6%, money doubles in 12 years. At 8%, 9 years. It cuts both ways: a 24% credit card balance doubles in 3.

t: Credit Card Interest Explained: What Your APR Really Costs
d:
The APR on your credit card statement is not just a number. It is a monthly bill.

A 24% APR works out to roughly 2% a month. On a $3,000 balance that is about $60 a month. Pay the full statement balance by the due date and you pay $0.

d:

Invest $500 a month for 30 years at an assumed 7%: about $610,000 with almost no fee, about $502,000 with a 1% fee. Check the expense ratio on every fund.

t: Credit Utilization Explained: The Fastest Credit Score Lever
d:
Credit utilization is the fastest lever on your credit score, and most people have never heard of it.

It is your balance divided by your limit. On a $5,000 limit, owing $500 is 10%. $1,500 is 30%, the usual ceiling. Pay the card down before the statement date.

t: Sinking Funds Explained: Stop Treating Bills Like Emergencies
d:
The holidays are not an emergency. Neither are car repairs. That is what sinking funds are for.

Set aside a small amount each month for a cost you can see coming. $600 of holiday spending is $50 a month. An $1,800 vacation is $150 a month.
